adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `def change` but contains multiple `execute(...)` calls (selects, inserts, and a delete). In Rails, arbitrary `execute` statements inside `change` are not automatically reversible, so `rake db:rollback` (or `db:migrate:redo`, which relies on rolling back) will raise an `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` unless wrapped in a `reversible`/`up`/`down` block. Additionally, `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop an existing `embeddable_hosts` table if present when the migration is applied, which can destroy data. The final `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` also removes settings data with no down-path to restore it.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — raw string interpolation `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` of legacy host values into SQL with no escaping; a host containing a single quote breaks the migration or corrupts data (SQL injection shape). [95, P1]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads legacy embeddable_hosts from the database (site_settings.value), splits it into lines, and then builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is inserted inside single quotes with no escaping/quoting helper, any host line containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will break the SQL and can alter the statement (SQL-injection-shaped). Even if the setting UI usually validates, this migration is operating on existing DB values and can fail/corrupt data if those values are not clean.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — same raw interpolation of `h` into INSERT with no escaping/parameterization; executes with migration/DB-owner privileges during upgrade. [100, P2]

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads `val` from the `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into `h`, then runs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is interpolated directly into SQL inside single quotes with no escaping/parameterization, any stored value containing `'` (or crafted SQL) can break out of the string and alter the statement. Migrations run with elevated DB privileges during upgrade, so this is a verifiable SQL-injection risk in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24 — migration builds SQL via raw string interpolation rather than `connection.quote`/parameterized insert; structural fragility independent of trust level. [100, P2]

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` builds an INSERT statement via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The interpolated `h` comes from `site_settings.value` split by newlines and is not quoted/escaped. If any stored host contains a single quote or other special characters, the migration can fail (SQL syntax error) or insert unintended data. Using `connection.quote(h)` / parameterization would avoid this fragility.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22-28 — `val.split("\n")` doesn't strip/filter blank/whitespace-only lines, silently inserting garbage empty-string host rows (satisfies null:false but not host format intent). [80, P2]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old setting `val` and does `records = val.split("\n")` then unconditionally inserts each `h` via raw SQL. If the old `embeddable_hosts` setting contains blank lines or whitespace-only lines (e.g., trailing newline), `h` can be `""` or just spaces. Because the migration bypasses model validations (uses `execute`), those invalid/garbage hosts can be inserted despite the model’s host format intent/validation. This is a concrete correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb — no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and no unique index in the migration; "one host → one category" invariant is unenforced, `record_for_host`'s `.first` makes duplicate-row resolution silently nondeterministic. [100, P1]

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `embeddable_hosts` table and `EmbeddableHost` model but does not enforce uniqueness of `host` either at the model level or via a DB unique index (migration only creates columns). Yet lookup/authorization and category selection depend on a single row: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record’s `category_id`. If duplicate rows for the same host exist, which is currently allowed, the chosen row/category becomes order-dependent and effectively nondeterministic. That is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb — no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`/DB unique index; duplicate host rows creatable via admin UI, untested. [75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` as the source of truth for allowed embed hosts, and host lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (no ordering) in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`. The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` without a unique index, and the model only validates format (no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`). The admin controller `create` endpoint also doesn’t prevent duplicates. This makes it trivially possible to create duplicate rows for the same host via the admin UI/API, leading to ambiguous/unstable behavior (which category gets chosen depends on whichever row `.first` returns). No tests cover duplicate handling. This is a real correctness issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-16 — `update`/`destroy` call `.where(id:).first` with no nil-guard before mutating/destroying; missing id causes unhandled NoMethodError (500) instead of 404. [100, P2]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-14 — same nil-guard-missing update/destroy issue, confirmed independently. [75, P2]

If no record matches the given id, `host` will be nil and this will raise a NoMethodError instead of returning a 404/appropriate error response. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10-16 — same nil crash; admin-gated so low severity, but can leak stack traces if consider_all_requests_local is misconfigured. [75, P3]
